question: Should OpenClaw expose post-subagent completion handling as a dedicated subagent hook, as part of a generic delivery/output boundary, or keep subagent lifecycle hooks observation-only with separate delivery-policy issues?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API affects plugin authority, sensitive child-session data, message delivery semantics, and compatibility with the recently rejected subagent-only guard-hook shape.

options.title: Generic Delivery Boundary
options.body: Design one plugin-facing completion/output boundary that can cover subagent completion review, filtering, and fallback notification with shared security and delivery semantics.

options.title: Dedicated Subagent Hook
options.body: Add a narrow post-subagent-completion hook with bounded payload and return semantics, accepting that it becomes a separate public contract from broader delivery/output policy.

options.title: Observation Only
options.body: Keep subagent lifecycle hooks observational and route suppression, fallback notification, and verification through narrower delivery-policy or plugin-runtime issues.

recommendation.title: Generic Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Design one plugin-facing completion/output boundary that can cover subagent completion review, filtering, and fallback notification with shared security and delivery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This person provided the latest explicit API-direction signal by closing the related guard-hook PR and naming the generic delivery-boundary direction.
